newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - Jan 15.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - Jan 15.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following stories on its front page on Wednesday:
- Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat sealed the long-delayed deal on a partial Israeli withdrawal from Hebron.
- New York Mayor Rudolph Giuliani proposed building a tunnel beneath New York Harbour to carry rail freight efficiently between the water-fringed city and the rest of the country.

- Rep Jim McDermott of Washington stepped down from the House Ethics Committee, seeking to still the controversy over his role in the publication of a tape-recorded conversation involving House speaker Gingrich.

- New York Governor George Pataki proposed a $66.1 billion budget that relies heavily on strong economic growth and cuts into higher education and health care programmes to finance additional spending on public schools and prison construction as well as a new round of tax cuts.

- Just weeks after the Swiss government ordered its banks to preserve any remaining records of their dealings with Nazi Germany, a suspicious security guard at the Union Bank of Switzerland halted the destruction of documents from the World War II era, including some that appeared to deal with the "forced auctions" of property in Berlin in the 1930s.
